subject: Acme Retail renewal — pricing adjustment, credits and uplift coordination
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@acme-retail.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal proposal and capacity uplift — Q3 go-live

Samir / Sarah,

Thanks again for the time earlier this week. Per our conversation, I attached an initial term sheet for Acme's upcoming renewal (Renewal_Term_Sheet_v1.pdf). High level:

- 12-month committed term (Apr 2027–Mar 2028)
- Baseline commit: 150M tokens / month, with a staged uplift to 250M tokens/month over Q1 post-renewal
- Unit pricing: $0.0009 per token (list), with options below for credits and a limited price-hold
- Proposed commercial levers: 1) one-time onboarding credit, 2) 60-day price-hold on list rate, 3) staged discount tied to commit cadence

We included an example uplift schedule and an ops checklist so your SRE team can plan the capacity increase. Would love to get your feedback on the commit cadence and whether Procurement needs an updated PO template.

Next steps I suggest:
- You confirm target baseline/peak commit and any contractual constraints from Procurement
- I loop in finance to formalize credit and price-hold language once we align on the delta to list price

Open to a quick 20-minute run-through next week.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
Rachel.kim@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0193

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme-retail.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@acme-retail.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal and capacity uplift — Q3 go-live

Rachel,

Thanks for the term sheet. A few immediate asks from our side:

- Can you tighten the price for year one? Our CFO is pushing for a stronger first-year discount versus the list of $0.0009/token.
- We need a 90-day firm price-hold after signing (rather than 60) to cover our procurement and forecasting cycle.
- Can the onboarding credit be applied against overage charges during the first 3 months of uplift? That would soften ops risk.
- Finally, we expect to confirm a baseline of 200M tokens/month and uplift to 300M tokens/month within 90 days — can you reflect that in a revised commit schedule?

Procurement (cc'd) will likely ask for an updated PO and invoice timing. If you can send a concession outline we can take to legal/finance this week, that would help accelerate.

Regards,
Samir Patel
VP, Platform Engineering
Acme Retail
samir.patel@acme-retail.com | +1 212-555-0188

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Acme renewal — customer asks for better first-year pricing and longer price-hold

David/Vanessa,

Looping you in — Acme wants a stronger concession on year-one pricing, a 90-day price-hold, and the onboarding credit to offset early overages. They plan to baseline at 200M tokens/mo and uplift to 300M within 90 days.

Questions:
- What's our flexibility on a time-limited deeper first-year discount (we want to protect unit economics)?
- Can we tie the onboarding credit usage to overages for the first 3 months operationally and still recognize revenue appropriately?
- Any approval thresholds I should flag (legal/finance sign-off required)?

I've attached Samir's note below for context. Planning to propose a concession that preserves a minimum effective price and is contingent on a 12-month commit + signed amendment. Thoughts?

Thanks,
Rachel

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 10:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Acme renewal — concession options

Rachel / Vanessa,

Thanks for the context. We can approve a limited concession that keeps long-term economics intact. Proposal to offer Acme: 

1) First-year effective discount: 18% off list for months 0–6, stepping to 10% months 7–12, contingent on a signed 12-month amendment and a 12-month minimum commit (200M tokens/mo baseline).
2) Price-hold: extend to 90 days post-signature (per Samir) for list rate; after 90 days, standard tiered pricing applies unless a renewal is triggered.
3) Onboarding credit: one-time $30,000 credit that can be applied to overage invoices during the first 3 months after uplift. Unused credit expires after month 3.
4) Uplift schedule: baseline 200M tokens/mo at signing, staged increase to 300M tokens/mo over 90 days; we will include an ops checklist and a 30-day runbook review to ensure no unexpected throttling.

Constraints / notes:
- Approvals: legal will need to sign the amendment form for the price-hold language; finance needs the HubSpot deal ID to record the credit.
- The effective discount structure protects our blended unit price vs. a flat deep discount.

If that looks sensible I'll ask Legal to prepare Amendment v3 (I can pre-clear the key commercial language).

-David

David Kim
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@acme-retail.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 16:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal and capacity uplift — updated concession and next steps

Samir / Sarah,

Appreciate the clarity — we've agreed internally on a concession package that should address Acme's procurement timing and early ops risk. Summary of agreed terms (attached Amendment v3):

- Commit: 12-month term; baseline 200M tokens/month with staged uplift to 300M tokens/month within 90 days of go-live.
- Pricing: effective 18% discount off list for months 0–6, then 10% months 7–12 (contingent on signed amendment and annual commit).
- Price-hold: 90 days from signature on list rate; after 90 days standard pricing ladder resumes unless the parties execute a renewal/amendment.
- Onboarding credit: $30,000 one-time credit, applicable to overage invoices during the first 3 months after uplift. Unused credit expires after month 3.
- Ops: joint runbook review within 30 days of uplift; Redwood will provide a capacity plan and dedicated SRE contact for the migration window.

Next steps: 
1) Rachel to share the DocuSign link for Amendment v3 (attached).
2) Acme to confirm PO timing and sign the amendment; Procurement contact Sarah to confirm invoice schedule.
3) Once signed, Redwood will schedule the runbook review and confirm the uplift milestones.

DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/mt/AcmeRenewal/DEAL-2027-0342
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/DE-342

If those items look right I'll mark the HubSpot deal as "Ready to Sign" and route to Legal for the amendment. Happy to jump on a 15-min call if you want to walk through the amendment language.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
Rachel.kim@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0193
